clue.text: The Censor is about to inspect a decorative strip

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so the censor's name goes round the other word

blocks.note: Cato the Elder, the Roman statesman famous as the Censor
to vet is to examine closely

explanation.surface: A stern censor is about to examine a strip of ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to inspect' does double duty in the surface; the inserted piece is a synonym of inspect, placed inside CA-TO to make CA-VET-TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavetto is a concave moulding, a quarter-round hollow used as an ornamental band in architecture.

clue.text: Appeared to produce letters containing page after page

something containing another item holds it inside, so the pages go within

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' looks like correspondence, but it means the letters of the word produce, rearranged to CRO-EDUP, with the two Ps going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To crop up is a phrasal verb meaning to arise or occur unexpectedly, so cropped up means appeared.

clue.text: Travelling expenses for one accepted by inspired amateur

indicators.note: what is accepted is taken in, so the single digit goes inside the other word

blocks.note: vatic means prophetic, inspired like a seer
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Travel allowances paid to someone taken on by a gifted beginner.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside VATIC after its first letter, then A follows: V-I-ATIC-A.
explanation.definitionFit: Viatica is the plural of viaticum, Latin for provisions or an allowance of money for a journey.

clue.text: PM overheard in the refreshment hut

explanation.walkthrough: The Irish title is said roughly 'tee-shuck'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taoiseach is the prime minister of the Republic of Ireland, head of its government.

clue.text: Something in the wind for him

definitions.text: Something in the wind for him

blocks.note: surface reading: a hint of something coming; setter's reading: a member of the wind section of an orchestra

explanation.walkthrough: 'Something in the wind' is an idiom for a rumour, but here it is the woodwind; the old English name hautboy contains 'boy', which is what 'for him' hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument, once known in English as the hautboy, from French for high wood.

clue.text: Keeps a chap's horse in grass

blocks.note: to keep something is to have it
something belonging to a man is his

explanation.surface: A man keeps his horse out to pasture in a grassy field.
explanation.walkthrough: The horse and grass look like a farmyard scene, but both are drug slang: horse is heroin (H) and grass is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass is slang for cannabis, and hashish is cannabis resin, so the slang term stands for the drug.

clue.text: Judges where this part work ends

definitions.text: Judges where this part work ends

explanation.walkthrough: Judges is the seventh book of the Old Testament, so the group of the first seven books ends there; 'part work' plays on a magazine issued in instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: The Heptateuch, from Greek for seven volumes, is the first seven books of the Bible, Genesis through Judges.

clue.text: Dramatic solo that is a send-up of an old Scots one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Send-up' looks like mockery, but in a down clue it turns ANE upwards to ENA.
explanation.definitionFit: A scena is an extended dramatic solo in opera, like a scene for one singer with recitative and aria.

clue.text: It is fashionable to stay near the coast

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay' looks like remaining somewhere, but it means support, as a shore is a prop.
explanation.definitionFit: Inshore means close to the land or towards the beach, as in inshore fishing or waters.

clue.text: Mount in Ebor Handicap's first spill

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of the word

explanation.definitionFit: Horeb is the biblical mountain where Moses received the law, often identified with Mount Sinai.

clue.text: A stock phrase in circulars for part of S. Island

clue.text: Work with the media, and get nothing right for a slave-driver

explanation.surface: Advice to deal with journalists and come away empty-handed, written for a cruel boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A slave-driver is a harsh master who works people mercilessly, which is exactly what an oppressor does.

clue.text: Divine writer, but no green pasture for him now

explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like an adjective, but as a noun it means a clergyman; the green pasture is a ley, removed from the end of PRIESTLEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A divine is a member of the clergy or a theologian, and a priest is an ordained minister of the church.

clue.text: Grave senator found here, perhaps

explanation.definitionFit: Catacombs are underground cemeteries of galleries with burial recesses, best known from ancient Rome.

clue.text: Oxford postmaster has some food first

1st, with I standing for the figure 1

explanation.definitionFit: Portionist is the historical name for a scholar on a foundation allowance at Merton, whose scholars are still called postmasters.

clue.text: Drop a play

taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play written for performance on stage, radio or television.

clue.text: In public, an English king has to do too much

explanation.definitionFit: To overexert yourself is to strain or tire yourself by making too great an effort.

clue.text: Detail can count in support of an article's conclusion

explanation.walkthrough: 'Detail' is a verb here, meaning to list item by item.
explanation.definitionFit: To detail is to set out particulars one by one, and to enumerate is to name things individually in a list.

clue.text: Inspired description of the Prince's soul

clue.text: Lady from Virginia who married Marmaduke Bonthrop Shelmerdine
